note: Spain finding (reviewer ruling on #23): in-sample, one race, no CI. none is flattered only through the SC factor (sc_lap_factor 1.36 was set on this race); the base delta is a common level the offset adjustment removes. The shrinkage loss at horizon 40-49 (k 17-26) is the first-stint wear/fuel identifiability window documented in #14. The losses at 10-39 suggest the race-fitted linear MEDIUM wear (0.068, pulled up by old-tyre curvature a linear model cannot represent) predicts remaining stints worse than the practice value (0.031): this points at the hinge degradation model for sprint 2, not at the shrinkage. Nothing is changed on Spain; taus, hinge and calibrator choice are selected across races by LORO. This is not evidence that race evidence hurts in general.
